content: Usually when I open mail, there are boxes next to each email that I can click to delete. content: My calnedar is frozen. On the left side is the month of October 2026. I click on the arrow to move to Novemebr or September nothing happens. title: Alert from added account: failure due to backend error
creator: juriyronzhin
content: Yandex email account. Messages are constantly being received: “Alert from account [redacted]@yandex.ru: UID fetch message 5 uid 122: failure due to backend error”. But these notifications appear almost every second. What is the problem?

title: How can I maintain email formatting during MBOX to PDF conversion?
creator: singhhvaibhav888
content: Maintaining email formatting is important when converting mailbox data into PDF documents. Emails often contain structured information such as sender details, recipient addresses, subject lines, timestamps, hyperlinks, signatures, and formatted message bodies. A basic copy-and-paste method may not preserve all these elements correctly. For example, images may shift positions, hyperlinks may disappear, and message formatting may change during the process. title: BUG su Thunderbird ultima versione Gmail Google Workspace IMAP inoltro posta inviata
creator: Michele_Wisdom
content:
Titolo: Inoltro "in linea" non funziona dalla Posta inviata (Gmail IMAP) — NS_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY in OpenComposeWindow

Ciao a tutti,

su Thunderbird 159 (Windows) con account Gmail in IMAP ho questo problema: l'inoltro "in linea" (inline) dalla cartella Posta inviata non fa nulla — nessuna finestra di composizione, nessun messaggio di errore a video.

Cosa funziona e cosa no: - Inoltro in linea dalla Posta in arrivo: FUNZIONA - Inoltro in linea dalla Posta inviata: NON FUNZIONA (silenzioso) - Inoltro COME ALLEGATO dalla Posta inviata: FUNZIONA

Errore nella Console errori (Ctrl+Shift+J) al click su Inoltra:

Uncaught (in promise) NS_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: Component returned failure code: 0x8007000e (NS_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY) [nsIMsgComposeService.OpenComposeWindow] 

   ComposeMessage chrome://messenger/content/mailCommands.js:443    _composeMsgByType chrome://messenger/content/mailCommon.js:898

Test già effettuati (tutti senza successo): 1. Proprietà cartella → Ripara cartella 2. Eliminazione manuale dei file .msf della Posta inviata (rigenerati al riavvio) 3. Copiati 5-10 messaggi in una cartella locale di test vuota: il problema persiste 

  (quindi NON è il volume della cartella)

4. Provato sia da pulsante che da menu contestuale

Workaround attuale: impostare "Inoltra messaggi: Come allegato" (Impostazioni → Generali), che funziona correttamente.

Nota: la firma di errore è identica al bug 2036765 (Forwarding/Redirecting fails with NS_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY), ma quello era su Exchange e risulta fixato in 151/152, mentre io lo riscontro su 159 con Gmail IMAP. Potrebbe essere una regressione correlata?

Grazie per l'attenzione. Michele

title: Are calendars supported over Graph API? Contradicting (?) information in wiki and release notes
creator: iyanmv
content:
Hello,

As far as I know, support for the Graph API only includes support for emails. This was clearly explained in the release notes of the first release that included support for this new API. It is also explained in the wiki (https://wiki.mozilla.org/Thunderbird:Microsoft_Graph_API):

"The Graph implementation should support all of the same operations as EWS. Thunderbird Exchange supported features. Calendar is not yet supported."

However, in the latest release notes the two new features are very confusing:

"Linux tray icons indicate unread mail and show its count in the tooltip"

How? I still don't get a tray icon, how would I see the email counter? Are you sure this is for linux and not for windows only? The new tray icon from 154.0 was only for Windows, despite many blog posts wrongly saying this was available in Linux. This is clearly explained here: https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/close-tray-starting-154

"Graph calendars are auto-detected on new account creation"

How? So are calendars supported over Graph? If so, they can only be added when adding a new account? What about previously set up accounts using Graph? This bullet point is so confusing when everywhere else (support articles, wiki linked above, etc.) all clearly say that Graph support does not include yet calendar support.

title: Thunderbird resets and redownloads all my emails everytime I open the program
creator: becky1
content: I am still running Windows 10, but as of yesterday every time I open Thunderbird it resets my settings and spends hours re-downloading every email that I have. It constantly tells me that the connection to the server has failed and that all my passwords are wrong. Nothing is wrong with the server and none of my passwords are incorrect. After about 2 hrs, it completely re-downloads every email (I have multiple accounts) and I can continue to work like nothing was ever wrong in the first place. However, if I close out the program, it starts all over again. It randomly picks an email account and requires that I start from scratch and reset them up. Other times they are there like nothing happened. I have restarted my computer multiple times, it continues to do this.

I cannot find a control or documentation which governs the time zone used by either the Date column or the message date in the right part of the message pane.

title: Thunderbird 153 ESR freezes during POP3 mail retrieval and while idle on Windows 10
creator: kawamtmy
content:
Hello, I am experiencing repeated freezes in Thunderbird 153 ESR on Windows 10. I have been investigating this problem since mid-October 2026, but have not been able to identify the cause. Thunderbird is essential for my daily work, so I would appreciate advice on identifying the cause and restoring stable operation.

1. System environment - PC: dynabook R63/B - OS: Windows 10, 64-bit - Thunderbird: 153.6.0esr, 64-bit - Mail provider: @nifty (Japan) - Incoming mail: POP3 over SSL/TLS, port 995 - Security software: Super Security (Japanese security software) - Mail storage: Local mbox files

2. When the problem started Thunderbird worked reasonably well until September 2026. The freezing problem began around mid-October 2026. Windows Reliability Monitor recorded Thunderbird as "Stopped responding" on October 19, 2026, at 9:48 a.m. This is the earliest recorded incident I have found, although the problem may have started earlier. Thunderbird update history: - September 18: 153.3.1esr - October 1: 153.4.0esr - October 14: 153.5.0esr - October 21: 153.5.1esr - October 28: 153.6.0esr The first recorded freeze occurred after the update to 153.5.0esr. However, I have not established that the update caused the problem.

3. Symptoms Thunderbird becomes unresponsive and usually has to be forcibly terminated. During these freezes, Windows Task Manager often shows Thunderbird using approximately 30–40% CPU, repeatedly around 39–40%. Freezes also occur when Thunderbird is using only about 1.1 GB of memory. On other occasions, memory usage has increased to approximately 2.56 GB. The problem occurs under several different conditions: 1. During manual POP3 mail retrieval. 2. After repeated manual mail retrieval operations. 3. Approximately 30 minutes after a single mail retrieval, even when Thunderbird is left idle. 4. Sometimes after replying to messages or copying messages to other folders. 5. In both normal mode and Troubleshoot Mode. 6. Sometimes during the first mail retrieval after starting Thunderbird. Other Windows applications generally remain responsive when Thunderbird freezes. Restarting Windows sometimes restores normal Thunderbird operation temporarily, but the problem returns.

4. Troubleshooting already performed I have already tried the following: - Reinstalled Thunderbird from the official website. - Created a new Thunderbird test profile. - Disabled extensions. - Disabled hardware acceleration. - Disabled global search and indexing. - Removed all active Thunderbird message filters for testing. - Disabled the anti-spam component of Super Security. - Disabled automatic mail checking and automatic downloading. - Tested manual mail retrieval in Troubleshoot Mode. - Reduced the size of the Inbox from approximately 4.1 GB to 2.4 GB. - Performed a full antivirus scan, which detected no threats. The new profile initially worked, including several successful POP3 retrievals, but the freezing problem later returned. Reinstalling Thunderbird did not resolve the issue. The anti-spam component remains disabled for testing, but the problem continues.

5. Windows error records Windows Reliability Monitor recorded Thunderbird as unresponsive on October 19, 2026, at 9:48 a.m. Windows Event Viewer also recorded an Application Hang, Event ID 1002, on October 30, 2026, at approximately 4:23 a.m. The affected executable was thunderbird.exe, version 153.6.0.0. These records confirm the application hang but do not identify its underlying cause.

6. POP3 communication Earlier POP3 logging confirmed that Thunderbird connected to the @nifty POP3 server and received a CAPA response. However, I have not identified which POP3 or internal Thunderbird operation was active at the exact moment of the freeze. I have not collected a process memory dump.

7. Potentially related Mozilla bug reports I found two reports that may be relevant: - Bug 2080699: POP mail retrieval becomes unresponsive in Thunderbird 153.4.0esr. - Bug 2031744: Freezing potentially related to mail index (.msf) files and background processing. Some symptoms are similar, but I cannot determine whether they have the same underlying cause.

8. Questions I would appreciate advice on the following: 1. Are there known POP3-related freezes or high-CPU problems in Thunderbird 153 ESR, particularly after the October 2026 updates? 2. Could background mail processing, folder maintenance, or mail index files explain a freeze that occurs while Thunderbird is idle? 3. Could interaction with antivirus software or Windows networking components cause these symptoms? 4. Are there diagnostic steps that can help identify the cause without repeatedly freezing Thunderbird or risking existing mail data? 5. Would this information be more appropriate as an additional comment on an existing Bugzilla report or as a separate bug report? I have already spent considerable time testing different configurations. I would prefer to avoid repeating tests that have not helped. I have a backup of my Thunderbird profile and would like to preserve my existing mail data.

Thank you for your assistance.

title: Why doesn't Thunderbird clear the "newly downloaded" bit when archiving a message?
creator: philipp27
content:
tl;dr: I'd like to argue that a user who executes the archive action has seen the email in question, and that executing this action means that the email is no longer "newly downloaded" and doesn't deserve the highest of visual markings anymore.

We're not talking about the read/unread bit here (the green dot and the grey numbers in the folder pane). We're talking about the "newly downloaded" aka. "new and unseen" bit (the yellow star/rhombus and the blue numbers in the folder pane).

When a new email arrives, it's marked as "newly downloaded" and the inbox lights up blue because of it. Fair enough. It's also unread, of course. I often archive emails right away without opening/reading them. But I have seen the subject line of course, and I have a pretty good idea of what the email is and why I don't read it. I have the message pane disabled, so I can easily select an email without it being displayed and being marked as read. In the past, I used the message pane combined with that "mark as read after 1min" setting.

Now when I archive the message, the archive folder lights up blue and when I go in there, the email that I just archived has a star/rhombus. But I don't want my archive folder to look interesting with a blue color only because I just moved an email into it. All the blue colors are supposed to be for things I haven't seen yet and still need to look at. In fact, any email I move to a place should not be able to make that place look blue. Blue color should be for things that appeared for other reasons.

I'm aware that switching folders (e.g. away from inbox and back to it) or restarting Thunderbird will clear this "newly downloaded" bit. But I'm not doing that. I stay in the inbox, I get emails, I read them or archive them immediately. And when a folder on the left lights up in blue (that can happen thanks to my filter rules), then I take a look at that one as well. My Thunderbird application runs for weeks.

title: Feature Request: Option to disable or customize the "Ctrl+Enter" Send shortcut
creator: hunterlin.ndfai
content:
Dear Thunderbird Development Team,

I am writing to share feedback and request an essential usability improvement regarding keyboard shortcuts in Thunderbird.

While drafting emails, I frequently trigger the Ctrl + Enter shortcut by accident. This causes unfinished emails to be sent out immediately, leading to awkward and unprofessional situations with recipients.

To resolve this issue, I attempted using add-ons such as tbkey-lite to remap or disable the shortcut, but the configuration proved ineffective. As a temporary workaround, I have enabled the "Send Later" / delayed sending feature so I can intercept accidental sends in the Outbox. However, this is only a band-aid solution and remains a constant source of anxiety while typing.

I kindly request that future versions of Thunderbird consider the following improvements: 

   Built-in Shortcut Customization: An option in the settings menu to disable, rebind, or customize global/composer shortcuts (especially Ctrl + Enter). 
   Confirmation Prompt Toggle: A built-in preference to prompt a confirmation dialog before sending (e.g., "Are you sure you want to send this message now?"), which would prevent accidental keystrokes from immediately dispatching drafts.

Thunderbird is a fantastic, privacy-respecting client that I rely on daily. Having better control over critical keyboard shortcuts would significantly improve the writing experience for many users who face the same frustration.

Thank you very much for your time, dedication, and continued hard work on this project.

Best regards,|

Hunter

I found an ESET setting was the culprit, in advanced settings under "email client setup" they have a toggle for "Scan IMAPS mail transport" by default this is on. From ESET's information this function scans the mail in route to the client. It does not affect "other" AV function with mail.

The Question: Should I pursue resolving this with TB? Or is it just a conflict?

content:
I'm running Thunderbird v. 153.6.0esr (64-bit) on my notebook computer desktop. Yesterday I attempted to re-add an e-mail account to Thunderbird after deleting it to update the settings for that account so that they'd properly align with my ISP's server settings for the account. This originally came about after I changed the account password a couple of times, and found myself unable to send e-mail from Thunderbird. I was, and still am, able to send e-mail from the ISP's webmail app, however.

I installed the update to the Program files folder, which was the default location. Immediately after upgrading, I noticed that the deleted user e-mail account was restored in Thunderbird. The account settings, including server settings, appeared to be correct. Upon closer inspection, I also noticed that the most recent e-mails saved in the inbox and in folders for the two accounts with the same domain name dated back to last year or earlier, even though I received many e-mails addressed to those accounts in Thunderbird since then I can't explain why that happened. Something else rather strange happened: Both the former Thunderbird installation v. 153.6.0esr (64-bit) and the new, upgraded installation v. 160.0 (64-bit) now appear on my Windows taskbar. The first couple of times I did the upgrade to v. 160.0 (64-bit), that version's icon vanished after a few minutes and I was left with the previous v. 153.6.0esr (64-bit). Today, however, I launched Thunderbird from the upgraded Thunderbird.exe app found in the Program folder, which accounts for why the upgraded app's icon still appears on the taskbar. Yet I can still run the previous version just as I could before the upgrade, albeit without the previously deleted user account I sought to restore.

Although what I described may sound like a blessing as I have my choice of versions to choose from right on the taskbar, Moreover, two related Thunderbird apps were restored as well following the upgrade: Lightning and my Address book, although with the same date limitations mentioned above concerning the e-mail files. This very much concerns me, especially because the e-mail files in the upgraded version appear to be outdated by, at first glance, four months to > 1 year. I'm also concerned because I thought the upgrade process would be automatic. This upgrade, however, was anything BUT automatic.

I find myself getting busier with work these days, and as we're nearing the holiday season. I simply don't have time to troubleshoot this now. I can use Thunderbird on my mobile phone without a problem. I don't wish to use it on the ISP's webmail app as it would simply be too inconvenient in the long run. Please help if you can, at least by offering or providing an explanation of why the above anomalies happened. Also note that I have a recent full image backup of my hard disk. I'll be glad to make screenshot images of this latest configuration available to you upon request.

I have one more, but related, request. If you know of a way I can restore the deleted user account I referred to above to my previous version of Thunderbird, 153.6.0esr (64-bit), let me know what that is and I'll gladly delete the new v. 160 I upgraded to. I'd like to be able to upgrade to that version smoothly and without the inconsistencies I encountered with this upgrade, but I recognize the need to do it without losing at least a year's worth of e-mail data, as described above.

title: Thunderbird having trouble with formatted text pasted from Google Docs when composing
creator: trlist1
content:
I am having some trouble with copy and paste when composing. The background here is that I never was a good typist, and I have some physical difficulties (essential tremor) that make typing more difficult now. My solution for this is to use Google Docs’ Voice Typing feature to dictate most of what I write. I often do formatting there as well.

If I then paste unformatted from Google Docs into the TB compose window things generally work pretty well. However, if I paste formatted text there are a number of problems. Some of this is because Google Docs is inserting far too much unnecessary junk into the HTML for the formatted text (I looked with HTML Source Editor). But some of it seems to be problems in TB, here are examples of some of the things I've seen:

  • Pasted text ends up being seen by Thunderbird as a mix of Paragraph and Body Text. When I highlight it and try to switch it all to Body Text basically the change is ignored, that is, sections of the text still remain in Paragraph format. This messes up line spacing.
  • Font changes in pasted text have similar oddities. Google's fonts and font sizes often don't match up with the ones I have set in Thunderbird, and if I try to highlight the pasted text and adjust the font size using Thunderbird's font controls, frequently nothing changes.
  • Vertical navigation in pasted text is sometimes broken. The main symptom is that using the down arrow to move the cursor down through the pasted paragraphs works until you get to the last paragraph, but then instead of going down into the signature it jumps back to the beginning of the message, so it is cyclical rather than simply continuing down. If I use the down arrow to go to the last line and then a right arrow to go character by character the cursor moves into the signature area as expected, it's only the vertical arrows that are weird.

Are these bugs that are worth documenting and reporting? Is the above enough info to reproduce them? Or is it too much to ask Thunderbird to handle pasted formatted text better than it does?

I am also happy to hear other suggestions for speech to text tools that would do a better job of solving the underlying problem. Google Voice Typing leaves a lot to be desired.

Thanks!

title: New Outlook.com account – SMTP OAuth2 fails with “SmtpClientAuthentication is disabled for the Mailbox”
creator: pl11
content:
Hello,

I recently created a personal Outlook.com account and configured it in Mozilla Thunderbird on Windows 11.

What works:

  • Receiving emails via IMAP in Thunderbird.
  • Sending and receiving emails through Outlook.com webmail.
  • Microsoft OAuth2 authorization completes successfully.

What fails:

Sending emails from Thunderbird consistently fails with an SMTP authentication error.

SMTP configuration:

Server: smtp-mail.outlook.com Port: 587 Connection security: STARTTLS Authentication: OAuth2 Username: user@outlook.com (anonymized)

Exact error from Thunderbird's Error Console:

535 Authentication unsuccessful, SmtpClientAuthentication is disabled for the Mailbox.

Followed by:

Error during AUTH XOAUTH2, sending empty response

500 Unrecognized command 'Length: 7'

Troubleshooting already performed: Verified all IMAP and SMTP settings. Enabled two-step verification on my Microsoft account. Confirmed that the SMTP username matches my Microsoft account's primary alias. Deleted and renewed the stored OAuth2 credentials. Tested both smtp-mail.outlook.com and smtp.office365.com. Temporarily disabled Bitdefender's Thunderbird extension. Confirmed that Thunderbird accepts Microsoft authentication cookies.

None of these steps resolved the issue.

Microsoft Support declined to investigate SMTP AUTH availability for my mailbox and referred me to Mozilla.

I found similar reports, including Mozilla Bugzilla issue #2071567.

Could you confirm whether this is a known limitation affecting newly created Outlook.com accounts and whether a workaround or fix is available?

Thank you.

title: Problem transferring files via activity manager to gmail
creator: donald.pymont
content: I have transferred all my virgin media mail and folder directories across to Gmail and all seemed fine to start with and activity manager was beginning to show a transfer of folders and contents. I made the mistake of dragging all my virgin folders over to Gmail in one go. and now I have all the folders showing in Gmail but they are now all empty and activity manager shows no activity taking place. title: Severe Thunderbird performance issues with Gmail IMAP — 3–6 GB RAM, high CPU, 30-second message opening, even after clean reinstall
creator: johnny.quide
content:
Subject: Severe Thunderbird performance issues with Gmail IMAP — 3–6 GB RAM, high CPU, 30-second message opening, even after clean reinstall

Hello Thunderbird community,

I would like to report a persistent and severe performance problem when using Thunderbird with Gmail IMAP accounts. After extensive troubleshooting, Thunderbird remains practically unusable.

System configuration

- Device: Microsoft Surface Pro 7 - Processor: Intel Core i7-1065G7 - RAM: 16 GB - Operating system: Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit - Storage: 238 GB SSD - Antivirus: Bitdefender Antivirus Free - Thunderbird: Current Windows release downloaded directly from Mozilla (Date: Nov 17, 2026)

Problem

Thunderbird initially works normally with a new, empty profile.

After adding my Google Workspace account, performance was initially acceptable. However, after adding my personal Gmail account, Thunderbird became extremely slow.

Observed symptoms:

- Opening an email regularly takes approximately 30 seconds. - Reopening an email that was already displayed is just as slow. - Even opening application menus or changing settings becomes extremely sluggish. - Thunderbird occasionally displays "Not Responding" for extended periods. - RAM consumption reaches approximately 3–6 GB. - CPU usage remains around 12–14%, even when Thunderbird is offline and supposedly idle. - During these episodes, total system memory usage reaches 74–90%. - Network and disk activity can be close to zero. - On one occasion, Thunderbird appeared to start downloading IMAP headers again after the initial synchronization had already completed.

Importantly, the problem persists even when the Activity Manager shows no ongoing synchronization or indexing operations.

Troubleshooting already performed

1. Initially used the Microsoft Store version of Thunderbird. 2. Removed large local IMAP message stores (approximately 27 GB), after making backups. 3. Disabled local offline message storage. 4. Disabled global search and indexing using "mailnews.database.global.indexer.enabled = false". 5. Tested plain-text message rendering — no improvement. 6. Tested Troubleshoot Mode — performance became substantially worse, approximately five times slower. 7. Completely replaced the Microsoft Store installation with Thunderbird downloaded directly from Mozilla. 8. Created a clean profile without importing the old mailbox databases or search indexes. 9. Confirmed that the new installation worked normally before configuring the mail accounts. 10. Reconfigured Google accounts using IMAP/OAuth2, again without downloading complete offline mailboxes. 11. Allowed IMAP header synchronization to finish completely. 12. Tested offline mode — slightly faster, but still unusable. 13. Used "about:memory" → Minimize memory usage — Thunderbird became temporarily unresponsive, with no lasting improvement. 14. Confirmed that the problem is not caused simply by insufficient hardware resources.

The problem returned despite the clean installation and new profile.

Additional observations

The deterioration seems closely related to adding and processing the personal Gmail account. The Google Workspace account alone initially appeared to work normally.

My Gmail accounts contain extensive mail histories with many folders and thousands of messages. However, full offline message storage is disabled.

The application's main interface remains sluggish even when it is not actively downloading messages.

Questions for the community and developers

1. Is this a known Thunderbird performance regression affecting large Gmail IMAP accounts? 2. Could IMAP folder handling or message-list processing cause this degree of RAM consumption and sustained CPU activity? 3. Why does the problem persist after header synchronization has finished and Thunderbird is offline? 4. Could this indicate a problem with Thunderbird's internal message databases, even in a new profile? 5. Are there known fixes or specific diagnostic steps that would help identify the affected component?

I am willing to provide anonymized screenshots of Task Manager and performance diagnostics if useful.

I wanted to use Thunderbird as a long-term alternative to Microsoft Outlook, but the current performance makes that impossible.

Any suggestions or confirmation of similar experiences would be appreciated.

Thank you.

It did manage to send an outgoing email, but then reported that it could not save a copy to the sent folder because of "file permissions". It seems to me that something I have done during this folder clean up process has messed up Thunderbird's normal operation, but I don't know what exactly I did, or what I can do to recover from it. title: Adding a calendar invite fails with "Processing message failed. Status: 80004005"
creator: mozilla869
content:
I'm reporting a recurring issue with Thunderbird's calendar integration. When I attempt to accept a meeting invitation received by email, Thunderbird displays the following error:

"Processing message failed. Status: 80004005."

The event is not added to my calendar.

The latest occurrence involves a Microsoft Teams meeting invitation sent by a Teams user. This is not an isolated incident. I previously experienced the same problem with another meeting invitation, and the error was reproducible.

My configuration:

Thunderbird with a Google Workspace account configured for both Gmail and Google Calendar.

Calendar connected using Thunderbird's native CalDAV integration, automatically configured when the email account was added.

CalDAV server: apidata.googleusercontent.com

No third-party calendar add-on.

Previous troubleshooting:

I confirmed that I can create events directly in Thunderbird and that they synchronize successfully with the Google Calendar web interface. This indicates that the calendar connection and write permissions are functioning normally.

During the previous failure, Thunderbird's Error Console reported:

calendar: CalDAV: Unexpected status adding item: 400

calendar: iTIP processing failed: "Server Replied with 400" nsresult: "0x80004005 (NS_ERROR_FAILURE)"

The previous invitation contained Microsoft-specific iCalendar properties, including X-MICROSOFT-CDO-*.

Current issue:

The same error has now occurred with another invitation, specifically for a Microsoft Teams meeting. Thunderbird displays the Accept, Tentative, and Decline options, but accepting the invitation fails.

It appears that Thunderbird's handling of Microsoft-generated calendar invitations is incompatible with Google Calendar's CalDAV implementation in certain circumstances.

This is particularly problematic because Thunderbird is my primary email and calendar application, and I regularly receive meeting invitations from people using Microsoft Teams and Outlook.

Having to use the Google Calendar web interface to accept invitation defeats the purpose of the integration.

Thank you.

content:
2026年11月4日以降、Thunderbirdでメールの送受信ができない状態が続いています。現在のPCと古いPCの両方で同じ症状が出ています。

Yahoo!メールは、ThunderbirdだけでなくYahoo! Webメールでも通常のメールを受信できず、送信もできません。Yahoo!からの自動通知メールは受信できることがありますが、外部から送った通常のテストメールは届きません。

Thunderbirdには新しいパスワードを入力済みです。セキュリティソフトをNTTのものに変更した後もしばらくメールは正常に使えていたため、変更直後の問題ではないと思われます。

この症状はThunderbirdの設定によるものなのか、Yahoo!やぷららのメールサーバー側の問題なのか、確認方法を教えてください。
